title: Freundsberg Castle & Museum Schwaz
name: Freundsberg Castle & Museum Schwaz
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Freundsberg in Schwaz: proud hilltop castle dating back to 1170 with a five-story Romanesque keep, castle church, and museum of the silver town.
beschreibung:
Overview

The proud Burg Freundsberg (often referred to as Schloss Freundsberg) crowns a prominent wooded ridge at an altitude of around 675 meters high above the historic silver town of Schwaz in Tyrol's lower Inn Valley (Unterinntal). Erected around 1170 by the powerful Lords of Freundsberg as their ancestral seat, the impressive fortress stands as an iconic landmark of the city and an outstanding monument to high medieval aristocratic culture. Offering sweeping views over the Inn Valley, the Karwendel, and the Kellerjoch, the castle pairs living regional history with authentic Tyrolean hospitality.

Keep, Castle Church & Silver Museum

The architectural core of the fortress is the massive, five-story Romanesque residential tower (keep) dating from the 12th century, whose meter-thick stone walls still reflect the defensive might of the knightly era. Inside the tower, the Museum der Stadt Schwaz houses an exquisite cultural-historical collection: highlights include original artifacts from the golden age of Schwaz silver mining in the 15th and 16th centuries, historic traditional costumes, guild antiquities, and the famous Schwazer Bergwerksordnung (mining code). Rising above the palas is the magnificent late Gothic castle church featuring an artfully carved Renaissance altar and rare frescoes. From the top gallery of the keep, visitors enjoy a glorious panoramic view over the rooftops of Schwaz old town and the vast historic mine spoil heaps.

Visit & Getting There

Schloss Freundsberg and the municipal museum are open from early April to late October from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays; closed in winter or available for special tours by prior appointment). Admission fees (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youth (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.00, small children free. Holders of the Silbercard receive discounts. Getting there by car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Vomp or Schwaz), follow the signs toward Freundsberg through Schwaz old town up the castle hill (free parking directly at the castle gate). On foot: A signposted panoramic trail leads up from the Schwaz town square to the castle in about 25 minutes. By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Schwaz station, followed by local city bus or walking.

Tips

Housed within the evocative historic masonry of the outer bailey is the popular tavern Schlossschenke Freundsberg: savor traditional Tyrolean hearty cuisine and fine wines in the leafy beer garden with panoramic views across the Inn Valley. The courtyards and the tavern are accessible with minimal barriers; the historic ascent up the keep is via wooden staircases.
